title: Ahjo Makerspace
lead: Ahjo is Kiviruukin lukio's shared space for making: a cross-curricular STEAM learning environment where ideas become models, prototypes and solutions.
opening: Kiviruukin lukio opens in autumn 2027. Ahjo's equipment, guides and safety instructions will be ready before that, and this page grows as they are completed.
description: Kiviruukin lukio's Ahjo Makerspace: the courses Ahjo 1 and Ahjo 2, a shared resource bank, Ahjo's upcoming equipment and safety.

courses.subtitle: Technology basics
topics: Getting to know the equipment and working safely
goals: work safely in Ahjo and use its equipment as you were introduced to it
model objects to measure and make them with a 3D printer
build simple circuits and measure them with a multimeter
program a microcontroller and use sensors and actuators
build and program a simple robot
document your work and assess how well it succeeded

lessons.title: Welcome to Ahjo
lessons.text: The space, the equipment and how we work; the rules and the induction.
lessons.example: Map Ahjo's equipment and pick one real problem you could solve with it during the course, such as gear for your hobby or a tool that helps you study.

lessons.title: Working safely
lessons.text: Hand and power tools, protective equipment and an orderly workstation.
lessons.example: A risk assessment as at a workplace: choose one machine, identify its hazards and write instructions someone else can work safely from.

lessons.title: Basics of 3D modelling
lessons.text: Basic shapes, joining and cutting in a modelling program.
lessons.example: Model an ergonomic handle, a case or a spare part for something broken and justify your design choices.

lessons.title: A model to measure
lessons.text: Dimensions, tolerances and fitting parts together.
lessons.example: Design a two-part joint (snap fit or hinge) and find by experiment the clearance at which the parts fit together.

lessons.title: From model to print
lessons.text: Slicing, print settings and using the printer.
lessons.example: An optimisation challenge: the lightest printed truss that carries 2 kg. Compare how infill, layer height and print orientation affect strength and material use.

lessons.title: Judging a print and 3D scanning
lessons.text: Print defects and how to fix them; scanning an object into a model.
lessons.example: Scan an object, repair the model and print a scale copy. How accurate is it, and where do the differences come from?

lessons.title: Circuits and components
lessons.text: Power source, resistor, LED and breadboard.
lessons.example: Size an LED's series resistor with Ohm's law, build the circuit and compare the measured current with your calculation. What happens without the resistor?

lessons.title: Measuring with a multimeter
lessons.text: Measuring voltage, current and resistance connected the right way.
lessons.example: Measure the current drawn by a phone charger, an Arduino and a motor in different situations and estimate how long a battery would power your device.

lessons.title: A first Arduino program
lessons.text: The programming environment, digital outputs and a blinking LED.
lessons.example: Program a reaction-time game that measures reaction time in milliseconds and computes the class's mean and spread.

lessons.title: Sensors and inputs
lessons.text: Button, light and distance sensors; conditions and loops.
lessons.example: Build a measuring device: a classroom CO₂, noise or temperature logger that records data. Plot a graph of a lesson's data.

lessons.title: Motors and actuators
lessons.text: Servo and DC motor; power supply and control.
lessons.example: Use a servo to turn a solar panel towards the light and measure how much power tracking adds compared with a fixed panel.

lessons.title: Soldering
lessons.text: Using a soldering station and soldering a small circuit.
lessons.example: Solder your measuring device onto stripboard so that it lasts. Test the joints with a multimeter and compare reliability with the breadboard.

lessons.title: Building a robot
lessons.text: The structure of a robotics kit, drive train and sensors.
lessons.example: Build a robot that carries a load around a course as fast as possible. Compare how the gear ratio affects speed and pulling force.

lessons.title: Programming a robot
lessons.text: Movement, sensor control and solving a task with a program.
lessons.example: Program a robot to find its way past obstacles with its sensors. Compare simple and proportional (P) control in line following.

lessons.title: Mini project
lessons.text: A small device of your own with the methods learned: design and build.
lessons.example: A small device of your own with the methods learned, such as a plant moisture monitor, a bike light system or a sports performance meter.

lessons.title: Presentation and self-assessment
lessons.text: Presenting and documenting the mini project and assessing your own learning.
lessons.example: Present your device as in a product review: goal, solution, measurements and what you would do in the next version.

courses.subtitle: Design and build
goals: define a problem and the user's needs
come up with possible solutions and choose between them with reasons
plan and schedule a project in a group
build a prototype with Ahjo's equipment and methods
test a solution and improve it on the basis of tests and feedback
document and present the project and assess your own and the group's work

lessons.title: Starting the project
lessons.text: How Ahjo 2 runs, teams and finding a project topic.
lessons.example: Look at a few student invention and enterprise projects and collect problems that matter to you, the school or the neighbourhood.

lessons.title: Defining the problem
lessons.text: Whose problem, what need, and how success is recognised.
lessons.example: Interview at least three users and write a precise problem definition: who, in what situation, and by what measurable criterion the solution succeeds.

lessons.title: Ideation
lessons.text: Ideation methods and producing several possible solutions.
lessons.example: Ideate through constraints: what if it cost at most €20, worked without electricity, or had to be repairable by the user?

lessons.title: Judging and choosing ideas
lessons.text: Criteria, comparison and a justified choice.
lessons.example: Rank the ideas with a weighted decision matrix that also covers sustainability: materials, energy use and life cycle.

lessons.title: Project plan
lessons.text: Goals, roles, schedule, materials and risks.
lessons.example: Write a plan with milestones, responsibilities, a budget and a risk assessment, as in a real product development project.

lessons.title: Design
lessons.text: Sketches, dimensioned drawings and digital models.
lessons.example: Make a dimensioned drawing and a 3D model from which another group could build the same part without explanations.

lessons.title: Materials and methods
lessons.text: Choosing suitable materials, equipment and ways of making.
lessons.example: Choose a material with reasons: compare strength, cost, making time and recyclability for at least two options.

lessons.title: A first prototype
lessons.text: A quick, simple model to try out the idea.
lessons.example: Build the smallest working prototype that tests the riskiest assumption of your project.

lessons.title: Testing the prototype
lessons.text: A test plan, measuring and recording observations.
lessons.example: Write a test plan: what is measured, how precisely, and what result counts as success. Collect the data and present it as a graph.

lessons.title: Feedback and improvement
lessons.text: Feedback from users and the group; planning changes.
lessons.example: Run a user test in which an outsider uses the prototype without instructions. Record what you see and decide what to change and why.

lessons.title: Building 1
lessons.text: Making the parts of the solution according to the plan.
lessons.example: Make the parts with different machines and share the work so that every member masters at least one new method.

lessons.title: Building 2
lessons.text: Assembling the parts; electronics, programming or finishing as needed.
lessons.example: Add a sensor, a microcontroller or a printed textile part that measurably improves how it works.

lessons.title: Final testing
lessons.text: Does the solution work: tests, measurements and comparison with the goals.
lessons.example: Test the final solution with the same measures as the prototype and judge whether the original goal was met.

lessons.title: Finishing
lessons.text: Last fixes, appearance and usability.
lessons.example: Finish it for presentation: a case, labels and instructions that let the user manage without the makers.

lessons.title: Documentation
lessons.text: The project's stages, decisions and results into a portfolio.
lessons.example: Put together a portfolio that tells your decisions and failures honestly; it also serves an upper secondary diploma and applications to further studies.

lessons.title: Presentation and assessment
lessons.text: Presenting the project and assessing your own and the group's work.
lessons.example: Pitch the project to an audience or a partner company and answer questions. Finally, assess your own and the group's work.

safety.title: Ventilation, protective equipment and fire safety

safety.title: What to do in accidents and dangerous situations
